Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the list of glycoproteins upregulated in IPMNS with both KRAS and GNAS mutations compared to wild-type IPMNs and explain the pattern with activities of signaling pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
In this study, glycoproteomics (Table S3I from Wang et al. 2025) was used to compare intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) harboring both KRAS and GNAS mutations versus wild-type IPMNs. Surgically resected IPMN tissue was macro-dissected, enriched for glycopeptides, and analyzed by LC-MS/MS; 85 significantly upregulated glycopeptides (FDR < 0.05, log2FC > 0) mapping to ~45 proteins were reported. Details such as sample size per contrast (“n”) or replicate number are not specified.

Keywords  
• O-glycosylation  
• Mucin biosynthesis  
• Glycosyltransferases  
• ERBB signaling  
• KRAS/GNAS mutations  

Candidate Genes  
MUC5AC, GALNT3, GALNT5, C1GALT1C1, ERBB3  

Pathway Enrichments  
Using preranked GSEA (hit_col="Protein", corr_col="log2FC") at relaxed FDR (0.5) yielded the following counts_by_database:  
– KEGG_2016: up 1, down 1 (50% up)  
– GO_Biological_Process_2023: up 3, down 0 (100% up)  
– Reactome_Pathways_2024: up 9, down 4 (69% up)  

KEGG_2016 (UP):  
| Theme                                        | Direction | Leading Genes   |
|----------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Mucin type O-Glycan biosynthesis (hsa00512)  | Up        | GALNT3, GALNT5  |

KEGG_2016 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                             | Direction | Leading Genes          |
|---------------------------------------------------|-----------|------------------------|
| Cell adhesion molecules (CAMs; hsa04514)          | Down      | GLG1, ITGA6, ICAM2     |

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP):  
| Theme                                  | Direction | Leading Genes                |
|----------------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------|
| Protein Glycosylation (GO:0006486)     | Up        | C1GALT1C1, GALNT3, GALNT5    |
| O-glycan Processing (GO:0016266)       | Up        | GALNT3, GALNT5               |
| Protein O-linked Glycosylation (GO:0006493)| Up    | GALNT3, GALNT5               |

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (DOWN):  
| Theme | Direction | Leading Genes |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| –     | –         | –             |

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes              |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------|
| Post-translational Protein Modification    | Up        | MUC5AC, GALNT3, GALNT5     |
| Metabolism of Proteins                     | Up        | MUC5AC, GALNT3, GALNT5     |
| Diseases Associated With O-glycosylation   | Up        | MUC5AC, GALNT3             |
| Diseases of Glycosylation                  | Up        | MUC5AC, GALNT3             |
| O-linked Glycosylation of Mucins           | Up        | MUC5AC, GALNT3, GALNT5     |

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                   | Direction | Leading Genes              |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------|
| Infectious Disease                      | Down      | ATP1A3, YWHAH, TLR8        |
| Viral Infection Pathways                | Down      | ATP1A3, YWHAH, TLR8        |
| SARS-CoV Infections                     | Down      | ATP1A3, YWHAH, TLR8        |
| Diseases of Metabolism                  | Down      | MUC5AC                     |
| SARS-CoV-2-host Interactions            | Down      | YWHAH, TLR8                |

Summary of Patterns  
1. Across all libraries, glycosylation-related pathways are the dominant upregulated signals: O-glycan biosynthesis (KEGG), protein O-linked glycosylation (GO), and Post-translational Protein Modification (Reactome) are robustly enriched (69–100% of enriched terms are up).  
2. Mucin biosynthesis stands out (MUC5AC, GALNT3, GALNT5): core mucin-type O-glycan machinery is selectively induced in KRAS/GNAS-mutant IPMNs.  
3. Non-glycosylation signals (e.g., cell adhesion molecules, viral/infection pathways) are weak or bidirectional.  
4. Classical KRAS/MAPK or GNAS-cAMP signaling modules (e.g., ERK, PKA) are not prominent in this glycoproteome contrast, suggesting a shift toward remodeling of the secreted/membrane glycoprotein repertoire rather than direct effector signaling in late-stage lesions.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtering the Reactome GSEA results for “Glyco” reveals:  
| Data Base              | Pathway                        | NES    | Lead Genes            |
|------------------------|--------------------------------|--------|-----------------------|
| Reactome_Pathways_2024 | O-linked Glycosylation         | 1.912  | MUC5AC, GALNT3, GALNT5|
| Reactome_Pathways_2024 | O-linked Glycosylation of Mucins | 1.912 | MUC5AC, GALNT3, GALNT5|

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)

Up-regulated glycosylation drivers  
| Gene      | Direction | Role/Function                                                                 | Pathway(s)                                             |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| MUC5AC    | Up        | Gel-forming mucin, extracellular matrix constituent; heavily O-glycosylated    | O-linked Glycosylation; Mucin type O-Glycan biosynthesis |
| GALNT3    | Up        | Polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 3 (initiation of O-glycosylation) | O-glycan Processing; Mucin type O-Glycan biosynthesis   |
| GALNT5    | Up        | Polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 5 (mucin-type O-glycosylation)    | O-glycan Processing; Mucin type O-Glycan biosynthesis   |
| C1GALT1C1 | Up        | Chaperone for core-1 β1,3-galactosyltransferase, builds core-1 O-glycan         | Protein Glycosylation                                   |
| GCNT1     | Up        | β1,6 N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase (core-2 O-glycan branch formation)          | O-glycan Processing; Protein Glycosylation              |

Down-regulated glycoprotein drivers  
No glycosylation-related leading-edge genes were found in significantly downregulated pathways at FDR < 0.5.

Comparisons & Confidence  
Glycosylation modules show coherent upregulation across KEGG, GO, and Reactome, indicating high confidence in a glycan-remodeling signature in KRAS/GNAS IPMNs. The absence of canonical RAS/MAPK pathway enrichment in this glycoproteome suggests that glycosylation changes may be a secondary adaptation rather than a primary KRAS effector signature.  

Implications  
Upregulation of mucin-type O-glycosylation enzymes and MUC5AC likely enhances mucin secretion and alters tumor–stromal barrier function, which could drive cyst-fluid accumulation and modulate immune evasion. These glycosylation changes could serve both as diagnostic biomarkers (cyst fluid analysis) and as therapeutic targets (glycosyltransferase inhibitors) in mutant IPMNs.

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Functionally validate whether GALNT3/5 upregulation alters O-glycan branch complexity on MUC5AC in IPMN cyst fluid.  
2. Test small-molecule inhibitors of GalNAc-T enzymes in IPMN organoid models to assess impact on mucin secretion and cell proliferation.  
3. Profile ERBB3 glycosylation status (N437) for effects on receptor dimerization and downstream signaling in KRAS/GNAS-mutant cells.  
4. Clarify the contribution of non-glycosylation pathways (e.g., ion transport/ER homeostasis) observed in ORA to lesion progression.
